name: execute_message_changes
title: Execute Message Changes
description: Apply exactly the changes prepared by prepare_message_changes: each message is edited or deleted in the customer's chat, and the team's copy in the dialog changes too. Each item reports its own result and its delivery, and delivery_counts totals the four statuses; ok: true means the messenger applied the change. Each message states its delivery: delivered (the messenger confirmed it), queued (in the sending queue, not delivered yet), unknown (the messenger may have accepted it and no answer will follow) or failed (it did not go out; the element is refused with the reason). Only delivered means it reached the customer: tell the owner that a queued message is waiting and that an unknown one may or may not have arrived, and never send either again. MESSAGE_NOT_FOUND means the message or the dialog is gone; MESSAGE_CHANGE_FAILED means the messenger refused and the message stays as it was; MESSAGE_CHANGE_INVALID means the new file can no longer be used and DIALOGS_SWITCHED_OFF that dialogs were switched off — nothing was changed for either; MESSAGE_CHANGE_UNCONFIRMED (delivery unknown) means the change may have been applied — read get_conversation before preparing it again. A preparation is applied once. Call this tool only after final human confirmation of the prepared scenario.

name: execute_reply_batch
title: Execute Reply Batch
description: Send exactly the batch prepared by prepare_reply_batch: each reply answers that customer's last message (a proactive item or an entity card is a new message), and the team sees a copy in the dialog. Sending never takes over a chat. Choosing the path: a personal text for each customer goes through prepare_reply_batch then execute_reply_batch; one identical message to a whole segment goes through broadcasts (create_broadcast). Each item reports its result and delivery; delivery_counts totals the four statuses; ok: true is delivered and nothing less. Each message states its delivery: delivered (the messenger confirmed it), queued (in the sending queue, not delivered yet), unknown (the messenger may have accepted it and no answer will follow) or failed (it did not go out; the element is refused with the reason). Only delivered means it reached the customer: tell the owner that a queued message is waiting and that an unknown one may or may not have arrived, and never send either again. REPLY_DELIVERY_UNCONFIRMED means the message is queued (delivery queued: its outcome shows in get_conversation) or its outcome is unknown (delivery unknown: the messenger may or may not have it and no confirmation will come) — either way do not send it again; REPLY_IN_PROGRESS means the reply is still going out — call again later with the same preparation; REPLY_BATCH_USER_WROTE_AFTER_PREPARE means the customer wrote again before a reply to their last message went out, so read the conversation and prepare again; ENTITY_CARD_NOT_FOUND (the entity is gone or unavailable) and ENTITY_CARD_NOT_OPENED (its target opens nothing for this customer) sent nothing; ENTITY_CARD_UNAVAILABLE means the customer got a short unavailable notice instead of the card, so do not send it again. Repeating the call with the same preparation returns the same results and resends only refused replies. A file still being prepared refuses the whole call; repeat it in a minute. Call this tool only after final human confirmation of the prepared scenario.

name: media_import_files

description: Import up to 10 media files into tenant storage and get media items (each carries a `media_ref`) for publish tools. ChatGPT fills `files` with the files the user attached. Other hosts pass `sources`, each with a `url`: an https address of the business site or an allowed file host, or, for a SMALL file you hold as bytes (up to 128 KiB decoded, such as an icon or a preview), data:<mime>;base64,<payload> together with its exact `byte_length` and optionally `sha256`; the type is checked against the bytes. A Claude chat attachment has no URL: the user uploads it in the web cabinet or the Mini App, or puts it on the business site and you pass that URL in `sources`. Local paths are not accepted. Optional `media_kind` (voice, audio, video_note) is checked against the bytes. Large files import in the background: COMMITTED returns the media items; IMPORTING returns an upload_id, then poll media_get_status(upload_id) until COMMITTED; STAGING means repeat this call with the same idempotency_key. One idempotency_key names one set of files: other files need a new key.

title: Site Get Analytics
description: Read the analytics for this business's own hosted site over a window of N UTC days, the last of which is TODAY. It returns total page views, tab sessions (the historical `views_unique` / `unique` names do NOT mean unique visitors), bot-link clicks, pages, referrer hostnames, UTM labels and click actions. Past days come from the nightly rollup; today is incomplete and is read from the live event buffer (`today` names that date; `live_stats: false` means the buffer could not be read, so today's zero is unknown, not "no visits"). `/x/` and `/x/index.html` are one page. Costs no tokens. Omit `days` for 7 days; requests above 30 days are bounded to 30. Optionally pass `page_path` to report one published page. The existing checksum Delta Sync writes only files whose bytes changed, so unchanged pages are not re-uploaded. 0-cost read.

Each `kind: "site"` page also carries `links` (`web`, `universal`, one `mini_app` per connected channel, each with a `description`): give the owner those links. While the page is not served `links` is empty and `links_recovery` says what to do. `mini_app_links` (per page, storefront pages included) and `mini_app_home` open the page or the home AS the Telegram/MAX/VK mini app, for a broadcast text; copy them, never build one yourself; `url: null` comes with a `reason`. `site_pages_set_visibility`, `site_delete_page` and `site_page_preview` take only `kind: "site"` pages. `protected` pages (platform files) cannot be hidden or deleted one by one; the home page `index.html` is an ordinary page. 0-cost read.

name: site_page_nudge_get
title: Site Page Nudge Get
description: Read the nudge setting of one published, visible site page (`id` from `site_list_pages`). A nudge is a timed follow-up: a person opened the page as a mini app and `delay_minutes` later has reached no goal. Returns `is_enabled`, `delay_minutes`, `step_id` (the funnel step sent first), `ai_enabled` and `ai_prompt` (the AI Manager task that follows the step), `goal_link_codes` and `ai_available` (false: the plan has no AI Manager). A page with no setting reads as disabled defaults. The platform storefront pages (shop, events, booking) are not site pages and cannot carry a nudge. 0-cost read.

name: site_page_nudge_set
title: Site Page Nudge Set
description: Replace the nudge setting of one published, visible site page (`id` from `site_list_pages`); the whole setting, not a patch. When a person opens the page as a mini app and reaches no goal within `delay_minutes` (5 to 10080, seven days), the business sends them the funnel step `step_id` (a step `id`, or null for none) and then, when `ai_enabled`, the AI Manager works on `ai_prompt` (1 to 2000 characters; the task for the AI, not a message to the person). One wait per person at a time: a second open of the page restarts the timer; another page replaces the wait only when its nudge is on with a step or AI and the person is not in the 30-day cooldown of that page. After a nudge the same person gets none on that page for 30 days. A goal ends the wait: any form submission of the person, any order, event registration or booking, and a tap on a goal link (`goal_link_codes`: codes of links the business owns, bare or `dl_…`, at most 50) set on any page of the business. A running wait uses the setting as it was when it started; but if the nudge is off or the page hidden or unpublished when the timer fires, the wait is cancelled (`superseded`, nothing sent). A live dialog does not block the step; the AI stays silent while an operator holds the chat and is skipped without tokens. `ai_enabled` needs a plan with the AI Manager. Refusals: SITE_NUDGE_PAGE_NOT_ELIGIBLE, SITE_NUDGE_DELAY_OUT_OF_RANGE, SITE_NUDGE_STEP_NOT_FOUND, SITE_NUDGE_GOAL_LINK_NOT_FOUND, SITE_NUDGE_AI_NOT_ON_PLAN, SITE_NUDGE_AI_PROMPT_REQUIRED. Stop with `is_enabled: false`: pending waits are cancelled when their timer fires.

name: site_publish
title: Site Publish
description: Step 2 of publishing: after every upload PUT completed, make the files under `upload_id` live at the ticket's `host`. The ticket's mode and base apply: `merge` keeps omitted files, the bio page, assets and references; `replace` removes omitted files. Only changed files are written, `index.html` LAST, so no half-swapped site shows. Access rules are set with `site_gate_set`, not by a file in the bundle, and a publish never changes them. A changed base or access policy is 409 SITE_BUNDLE_STALE: request a new ticket, PUT, publish again; another host is refused. Plan size limits are checked on the uploaded bytes; an HTML tag over the fixed size is SITE_HTML_TAG_TOO_LARGE with `path`, `tag`, `attr` in `details`: move the data into its own file and publish again. A refusal leaves the live site as it was.
